# Rapise

> This is the combined full documentation. Individual sections available at llms-*.txt


> Rapise is an automated software testing tool for desktop, web, mobile, and API testing. It uses RVL (Rapise Visual Language) and JavaScript for test automation.

Rapise documentation is organized into sections for different aspects of the tool.

## LLM-Optimized Documentation

- [llms-global.txt](llms-global.txt): Global utilities and Tester assertions
- [llms-web.txt](llms-web.txt): Web testing with Selenium/WebDriver
- [llms-rvl.txt](llms-rvl.txt): RVL (Rapise Visual Language) syntax and concepts
- [llms-framework.txt](llms-framework.txt): Test framework structure and files
- [llms-extending.txt](llms-extending.txt): Creating page objects and extension libraries

## Full Documentation

- Documentation: https://rapisedoc.inflectra.com/
- Getting Started: https://rapisedoc.inflectra.com/Intro/overview/
- User Guide: https://rapisedoc.inflectra.com/Guide/
- RVL Reference: https://rapisedoc.inflectra.com/RVL/
- API Reference: https://rapisedoc.inflectra.com/Libraries/
- AI Features: https://rapisedoc.inflectra.com/AI/

## Quick Reference

### Object Interaction Pattern

```javascript
// Standard action (logs to report, fails test on error)
SeS("ObjectId").DoClick();

// Silent action (no report, no test failure on error)
SeS("ObjectId")._DoClick();
```

### Common Global Functions

```javascript
Global.DoSleep(1000);                    // Pause 1 second
Global.GetProperty("key", "default");    // Read config value
Tester.Assert("message", condition);     // Assert with report
Tester.Message("info");                  // Log to report
```

### RVL Structure

RVL scripts are Excel spreadsheets with 7 columns:
Flow | Type | Object | Action | ParamName | ParamType | ParamValue

### Web Element Discovery

```javascript
Navigator.SeSFind("//button[@id='save']");     // XPath, retries, fails test
Navigator.Find("//button[@id='save']");        // XPath, single attempt, returns null
Navigator.DoWaitFor("//input", 5000);          // Wait up to 5s for element
```

================================================================================

# Rapise Global Objects and Tester API

This document covers the `Global` and `Tester` objects - always available in any Rapise test without recording or learning.

## Global Object

Utility functions not tied to a specific UI object.

### Global.DoSleep(ms)

Pauses test execution for specified milliseconds.

```javascript
Global.DoSleep(1000);  // Wait 1 second
Global.DoSleep(500);   // Wait 500ms
```

### Global.GetProperty(name, defaultValue, configPath)

Reads a property value from configuration file.

```javascript
// Read from default Config.json in test folder
var url = Global.GetProperty("BaseUrl", "http://localhost");

// Read from specific Excel config file
var user = Global.GetProperty("Username", "", "%WORKDIR%\\Shared\\Config.xlsx");
```

### Global.SetProperty(name, value, configPath)

Writes a property value to configuration file.

```javascript
Global.SetProperty("LastRunDate", new Date().toISOString());
Global.SetProperty("Token", token, "%WORKDIR%\\Shared\\Config.xlsx");
```

### Global.DoEncrypt(plainText)

Encrypts text for secure storage (e.g., passwords in config files).

```javascript
var encrypted = Global.DoEncrypt("myPassword123");
// Returns something like: "RkdINXpxNHVKM2FnZnk="
```

### Global.DoDecrypt(encryptedText)

Decrypts previously encrypted text.

```javascript
var password = Global.DoDecrypt("RkdINXpxNHVKM2FnZnk=");
// Returns: "myPassword123"
```

### Global.GetFullPath(relativePath)

Converts relative path to absolute using test's working directory.

```javascript
var fullPath = Global.GetFullPath("Data\\input.xlsx");
// Returns: "C:\Tests\MyTest\Data\input.xlsx"
```

### Global.DoLaunch(cmdLine, wrkDir)

Launches an external application.

```javascript
Global.DoLaunch("notepad.exe");
Global.DoLaunch("chrome.exe https://example.com", "C:\\Program Files\\Google\\Chrome");
```

### Global.DoWaitFor(objectId, timeout, pollInterval)

Waits for a learned object to become available.

```javascript
Global.DoWaitFor("LoginButton", 10000);  // Wait up to 10 seconds
```

---

## Tester Object

Assertions and reporting functions. All assertions write to the test report.

### Tester.Assert(message, condition)

Basic assertion - checks if condition is true.

```javascript
Tester.Assert("User is logged in", isLoggedIn);
Tester.Assert("Count is positive", count > 0);
```

### Tester.AssertEqual(message, expected, actual)

Compares two values for equality.

```javascript
Tester.AssertEqual("Page title matches", "Home", pageTitle);
Tester.AssertEqual("Item count", 5, items.length);
```

### Tester.AssertContains(message, str, substr)

Checks if string contains a substring.

```javascript
Tester.AssertContains("Error message shown", errorText, "invalid");
```

### Tester.Message(text)

Writes informational message to report (not pass/fail).

```javascript
Tester.Message("Starting login sequence");
Tester.Message("Found " + count + " items");
```

---

## Soft Assertions

Soft assertions record failures but don't stop test execution. Use for multiple verifications where you want all results.

### Tester.SoftAssert(message, condition)

```javascript
Tester.SoftAssert("Field A valid", fieldA !== "");
Tester.SoftAssert("Field B valid", fieldB !== "");
Tester.SoftAssert("Field C valid", fieldC !== "");
// Test continues even if some fail
```

### Tester.SoftAssertEqual(message, expected, actual)

```javascript
Tester.SoftAssertEqual("Name", "John", actualName);
Tester.SoftAssertEqual("Age", 30, actualAge);
```

### Tester.SoftAssertAll(message)

Fails the test if any previous soft assertions failed.

```javascript
Tester.SoftAssert("Check 1", cond1);
Tester.SoftAssert("Check 2", cond2);
Tester.SoftAssertAll("All validations passed");  // Fails if any above failed
```

---

## Report Control

### Tester.SuppressReport(flag)

Temporarily suppresses report output. Useful for hiding sensitive data like passwords.

```javascript
// Hide password entry from report
Tester.SuppressReport(true);
SeS("PasswordField").DoSetText(password);
Tester.SuppressReport(false);

// Alternative: use underscore prefix (also hides from report)
SeS("PasswordField")._DoSetText(password);
```

### Tester.SetReportAttribute(name, value)

Sets persistent attribute for subsequent report entries.

```javascript
Tester.SetReportAttribute("Module", "Checkout");
// All subsequent entries will have Module=Checkout
```

---

## Additional Tester Assertions

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `Tester.AssertFalse(msg, val)` | Checks val is false |
| `Tester.AssertNull(msg, val)` | Checks val is null |
| `Tester.AssertNotNull(msg, val)` | Checks val is not null |
| `Tester.AssertGreater(msg, n1, n2)` | Checks n1 > n2 |
| `Tester.AssertLess(msg, n1, n2)` | Checks n1 < n2 |
| `Tester.AssertStartsWith(msg, str, prefix)` | Checks str starts with prefix |
| `Tester.AssertEndsWith(msg, str, suffix)` | Checks str ends with suffix |

## Additional Tester Soft Assertions

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `Tester.SoftAssertFalse(msg, val)` | Checks val is false |
| `Tester.SoftAssertNull(msg, val)` | Checks val is null |
| `Tester.SoftAssertNotNull(msg, val)` | Checks val is not null |
| `Tester.SoftAssertGreater(msg, n1, n2)` | Checks n1 > n2 |
| `Tester.SoftAssertLess(msg, n1, n2)` | Checks n1 < n2 |
| `Tester.SoftAssertStartsWith(msg, str, prefix)` | Checks str starts with prefix |
| `Tester.SoftAssertEndsWith(msg, str, suffix)` | Checks str ends with suffix |

---

## Spreadsheet Object

Read and write Excel (.xls, .xlsx) and CSV (.csv, .txt) files. Essential for data-driven testing.

### Spreadsheet.DoAttach(fileName, sheetName)

Loads a spreadsheet file.

```javascript
// Load Excel file (first sheet)
Spreadsheet.DoAttach("%WORKDIR%\\Data\\TestData.xlsx");

// Load specific sheet
Spreadsheet.DoAttach("%WORKDIR%\\Data\\TestData.xlsx", "Users");

// Load CSV file
Spreadsheet.DoAttach("%WORKDIR%\\Data\\input.csv");
```

### Spreadsheet.GetCell(columnId, rowId)

Gets cell value. Column can be index (0-based) or name. Row is 0-based index.

```javascript
// By column index and row index
var value = Spreadsheet.GetCell(0, 1);  // First column, second row

// By column name and row index (row 0 contains headers)
var username = Spreadsheet.GetCell("Username", 1);
var password = Spreadsheet.GetCell("Password", 1);
```

### Spreadsheet.GetRowCount()

Returns total row count including header row.

```javascript
var rowCount = Spreadsheet.GetRowCount();
// Iterate data rows (skip header at row 0)
for (var i = 1; i < rowCount; i++) {
    var user = Spreadsheet.GetCell("Username", i);
    var pass = Spreadsheet.GetCell("Password", i);
    // ... use data
}
```

### Spreadsheet.DoSequential() / GetEOF()

Iterate rows using cursor. First row (headers) is skipped automatically.

```javascript
Spreadsheet.DoAttach("%WORKDIR%\\Data\\TestData.xlsx");
while (!Spreadsheet.GetEOF()) {
    var user = Spreadsheet.GetCell("Username");  // Gets from current row
    var pass = Spreadsheet.GetCell("Password");
    
    // Use data...
    Login(user, pass);
    
    Spreadsheet.DoSequential();  // Move to next row
}
```

### Spreadsheet.SetCell(value, columnId, rowId) / DoSave()

Write values and save changes.

```javascript
Spreadsheet.DoAttach("%WORKDIR%\\Data\\Results.xlsx");
Spreadsheet.SetCell("PASS", "Status", 1);
Spreadsheet.SetCell(new Date().toString(), "Timestamp", 1);
Spreadsheet.DoSave();
```

### Quick Reference

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `DoAttach(file, sheet)` | Load spreadsheet |
| `GetCell(col, row)` | Get cell value |
| `SetCell(val, col, row)` | Set cell value |
| `GetRowCount()` | Total rows (including header) |
| `GetColumnCount()` | Total columns |
| `DoSequential()` | Move to next row |
| `GetEOF()` | True if past last row |
| `DoSave(file)` | Save changes |

---

## Example: Complete Test Flow

```javascript
function Test(params)
{
    var config = Global.GetProperty("TestConfig", "default");
    
    Tester.Message("Starting registration with config: " + config);
    
    var username = "user_" + Date.now();
    SeS("UsernameField").DoSetText(username);
    SeS("PasswordField").DoSetText(Global.DoDecrypt(encryptedPwd));
    SeS("SubmitButton").DoClick();
    
    Global.DoSleep(2000);  // Wait for response
    
    // Verify
    var welcomeText = SeS("WelcomeMessage").GetText();
    Tester.AssertContains("Welcome message shown", welcomeText, username);
}
```

================================================================================

# Rapise Web Testing API

This document covers web automation using Selenium WebDriver in Rapise.

## Important: API Context

Rapise test code runs in a **test engine context**, NOT inside a browser. You cannot use browser DOM APIs directly:

```javascript
// WRONG - browser DOM APIs don't work
var text = element.textContent;           // ERROR
var attr = element.getAttribute("href");  // ERROR

// CORRECT - use Rapise wrapper methods
var text = element.GetText();
var attr = element._DoDOMGetAttribute("href");

// CORRECT - use WebDriver.ExecuteScript for raw browser JS
var checked = WebDriver.ExecuteScript("return arguments[0].checked", obj.element.e);
```

---

## Navigator - Finding Elements

### Navigator.SeSFind(locator)

Finds element with multiple retry attempts. **Fails the test** if not found.

```javascript
var btn = Navigator.SeSFind("//button[@id='save']");
btn.DoClick();
```

### Navigator.Find(locator)

Single attempt to find element. Returns `null` if not found (no test failure).

```javascript
var popup = Navigator.Find("//div[@class='popup']");
if (popup) {
    popup.DoClick();
}
```

### Navigator.DoWaitFor(locator, timeout)

Polls for element until found or timeout. Returns element or `null`.

```javascript
var spinner = Navigator.DoWaitFor("//div[@class='loading']", 10000);
```

---

## Navigator - Object State Checks

These methods check object state without failing the test. They accept either an object ID from the repository or an XPath (detected by leading `.` or `/`).

### Navigator.CheckObjectExists(xpathOrObjId)

Checks if object is found on the screen. Returns `true` if exists, `false` otherwise.

```javascript
var exists = Navigator.CheckObjectExists("//button[@name='Next']");
Tester.Assert("Next button exists", exists);

// Or with object ID from repository
var exists = Navigator.CheckObjectExists("LoginButton");
```

### Navigator.CheckObjectVisible(xpathOrObjId)

Checks if object is visible on the screen (exists and not hidden). Returns `true` if visible, `false` otherwise.

```javascript
var visible = Navigator.CheckObjectVisible("//div[@class='modal']");
Tester.Assert("Modal is visible", visible);
```

### Navigator.CheckObjectEnabled(xpathOrObjId)

Checks if object is enabled (exists and not disabled). Returns `true` if enabled, `false` otherwise.

```javascript
var enabled = Navigator.CheckObjectEnabled("//button[@id='submit']");
Tester.Assert("Submit button is enabled", enabled);
```

---

## Locator Syntax

Rapise supports multiple locator strategies with extensions for iframes, Shadow DOM, and visibility filtering.

### XPath (default)

```javascript
Navigator.SeSFind("//button[@name='Submit']");
Navigator.SeSFind("//input[@type='text' and @placeholder='Search']");
Navigator.SeSFind("//div[contains(@class,'active')]//span[text()='OK']");
```

### CSS Selector

Prefix with `css=`:

```javascript
Navigator.SeSFind("css=button.primary:visible");
Navigator.SeSFind("css=input[data-testid='email']");
```

### Iframe Boundary

Use `@@@` to cross into iframe:

```javascript
Navigator.SeSFind("//iframe[@id='editor']@@@//input[@name='content']");
```

### Shadow DOM Piercing

Rapise supports Shadow DOM in two ways:

**1. Automatic Piercing (Rapise 8.2+)**

CSS selectors automatically pierce open Shadow DOM boundaries - no special syntax needed:

```javascript
// These work even if the input is inside a shadow root
Navigator.SeSFind("css=input[id='editField']");
Navigator.SeSFind("css=guid-generator input");
Navigator.SeSFind("css=guid-generator > input");
```

**2. Explicit Boundary Crossing (`@#@`)**

For explicit shadow root traversal, use the `@#@` delimiter. The first part locates the shadow host (XPath or CSS), the second part (CSS only) finds elements inside:

```javascript
// XPath to shadow host, then CSS inside shadow DOM
Navigator.SeSFind("//guid-generator@#@css=input");

// CSS for both parts
Navigator.SeSFind("css=guid-generator@#@css=input:first-of-type");
```

Note: XPath doesn't work inside shadow roots - always use CSS after `@#@`.

### Visibility Pseudo-Classes

Rapise extends CSS with `:visible` and `:hidden` pseudo-classes (similar to jQuery):

```javascript
// Click only the visible Submit button (ignore hidden duplicates)
Navigator.SeSFind("css=button.btn-submit:visible");

// Select visible dropdown items after hover
Navigator.SeSFind("css=.dropdown-menu li:visible");

// Find the active/visible tab panel
Navigator.SeSFind("css=.tab-pane:visible");

// Verify loading spinner is hidden
Navigator.SeSFind("css=.loading-spinner:hidden");
```

An element is **hidden** if:
- `display: none`
- `visibility: hidden`  
- `opacity: 0`

An element is **visible** if none of the above apply.

Use cases:
- Dropdowns, tooltips, popups that appear on hover/click
- Tab interfaces where only one panel is visible
- Modal dialogs and backdrop elements
- Loading indicators and progress overlays

---

## Element Actions

Once you have an element, use these methods:

### Mouse Actions

```javascript
obj.DoClick();           // Click (smart - waits for element, auto-scrolls)
obj.DoClick(10, 5);      // Click at offset (x=10, y=5) from top-left
obj.DoDblClick();        // Double click
obj.DoDblClick(10, 5);   // Double click at offset
obj.DoRClick();          // Right click (context menu)
obj.DoRClick(10, 5);     // Right click at offset
obj.DoLClick();          // Direct click via JavaScript (bypasses visibility checks)
obj.DoMouseMove();       // Hover over element (move mouse to center)
obj.DoMouseMove(10, 5);  // Hover at specific offset
```

### Text Input

```javascript
obj.DoSetText("Hello");      // Clear and type text
obj.DoSendKeys("text");      // Send keystrokes (for file inputs, special keys)
obj.DoSelect("Option 1");    // Select dropdown option by visible text
```

### Reading Values

```javascript
var text = obj.GetText();    // Get visible text content
var tag = obj.GetTag();      // Get HTML tag name ("input", "div", etc.)
var width = obj.GetWidth();  // Get element width in pixels
```

### Visibility

```javascript
obj.DoEnsureVisible();       // Scroll element into viewport
```

---

## Underscore Prefix Convention

Every action has an underscore variant that:
- Does NOT write to test report
- Does NOT fail test on error

```javascript
// Standard - reports action, fails test if button not found
SeS("SaveButton").DoClick();

// Silent - no report entry, returns false if fails
SeS("OptionalPopup")._DoClick();
```

**Best practice**: Use underscore for intermediate steps, regular for final meaningful actions:

```javascript
// Intermediate navigation (underscore)
obj._DoEnsureVisible();
obj._DoMouseMove();

// Final action (regular - reported)
obj.DoClick();
```

---

## DOM Query Methods

### obj._DoDOMGetAttribute(attrName)

Read DOM attribute value:

```javascript
var href = link._DoDOMGetAttribute("href");
var title = span._DoDOMGetAttribute("title");
var dataId = div._DoDOMGetAttribute("data-id");
```

### obj._DoDOMQueryXPath(relativeXpath)

Find descendant elements using relative XPath (must start with `.`):

```javascript
var table = Navigator.SeSFind("//table[@id='results']");
var rows = table._DoDOMQueryXPath(".//tr");
if (rows && rows.length) {
    rows[0].DoClick();
}

// Find buttons inside a container
var container = Navigator.SeSFind("//div[@class='toolbar']");
var buttons = container._DoDOMQueryXPath(".//button");
```

---

## WebDriver Object

Low-level Selenium WebDriver access.

### WebDriver.ExecuteScript(script, ...args)

Execute JavaScript in browser context:

```javascript
// Check checkbox state
var isChecked = WebDriver.ExecuteScript("return arguments[0].checked", obj.element.e);

// Scroll to bottom of page
WebDriver.ExecuteScript("window.scrollTo(0, document.body.scrollHeight)");

// Get computed style
var color = WebDriver.ExecuteScript(
    "return window.getComputedStyle(arguments[0]).color", 
    obj.element.e
);
```

### WebDriver.Actions()

Build action chains:

```javascript
// Press Enter key
WebDriver.Actions().SendKeys('\uE007').Perform();

// Press Tab
WebDriver.Actions().SendKeys('\uE004').Perform();

// Press Escape
WebDriver.Actions().SendKeys('\uE00C').Perform();
```

### WebDriver.autoWait

Controls automatic page-load waiting. Disable for actions that shouldn't wait:

```javascript
// File upload pattern
var aw = WebDriver.autoWait;
WebDriver.autoWait = false;
fileInput.DoSendKeys(Global.GetFullPath("Data\\file.pdf"));
WebDriver.autoWait = aw;
```

---

## Page Object Pattern

Organize reusable actions in page objects.

**Naming convention**: Functions starting with `Do` are reported as actions. When `DoClickButton` returns `false`, Rapise treats it as a failed action automatically.

**Underscore usage**: Use `_DoClick()` and `_DoSetText()` inside page object methods to avoid duplicate report entries - the outer `DoClickButton` is already reported.

```javascript
// In PageObjects/MyApp/MyApp.js

SeSPageObject("MyApp");

// DoClickButton - reported action, failure auto-detected via return value
function MyApp_DoClickButton(/**string*/ name)
{
    var xpath = "//button[@name='" + name + "']"
        + "|//button[normalize-space(.)='" + name + "']";
    var obj = Navigator.SeSFind(xpath);
    if (obj) {
        obj.object_name = name;  // Shows "Save" instead of XPath in report
        return obj._DoClick();   // Underscore: don't double-report
    }
    return false;  // Returning false fails the DoClickButton action
}

// DoSetField - same pattern
function MyApp_DoSetField(/**string*/ name, /**string*/ value)
{
    var labelCond = "normalize-space(.)='" + name + "' or normalize-space(.)='*" + name + "'";
    var xpath = "//input[@id=//label[" + labelCond + "]/@for]";
    var obj = Navigator.SeSFind(xpath);
    if (obj) {
        obj.object_name = name;
        return obj._DoSetText(value);
    }
    return false;
}
```

Usage in tests:

```javascript
MyApp.DoClickButton("Save");    // Report shows: MyApp.DoClickButton("Save") - Pass/Fail
MyApp.DoSetField("Username", "john");
```

---

## Object Repository (SeS)

Learned objects are stored in `Objects.js` and accessed via `SeS()`:

```javascript
// Objects.js contains learned object definitions
saved_script_objects = {
    "LoginButton": {
        "object_type": "HTMLObject",
        "xpath": "//button[@id='login']",
        // ... other properties
    }
};

// Usage in test
SeS("LoginButton").DoClick();
SeS("UsernameField").DoSetText("admin");
```

---

## Retry/Wait Patterns

### Custom Auto-Wait Pattern

```javascript
function CustomAutoWait(fn) {
    for (var i = 0; i < 10; i++) {  // 10 attempts
        var result = fn();
        if (result) return result;
        Global.DoSleep(500);  // Wait between attempts
    }
    return null;
}

// Usage: wait for dynamic content
CustomAutoWait(function() {
    var el = Navigator.Find("//div[@class='loaded']");
    return el && el.GetText() === "Ready";
});
```

### Verify with Retry

```javascript
function VerifyField(name, expected) {
    var xpath = "//span[@data-field='" + name + "']";
    var actual = "";
    
    CustomAutoWait(function() {
        var obj = Navigator.Find(xpath);
        if (obj) {
            actual = obj.GetText();
            return actual === expected;
        }
        return false;
    });
    
    Tester.AssertEqual("Field " + name, expected, actual);
}
```

---

## Keyboard Constants

For `WebDriver.Actions().SendKeys()`:

| Key | Code |
|-----|------|
| Enter | `'\uE007'` |
| Tab | `'\uE004'` |
| Escape | `'\uE00C'` |
| Backspace | `'\uE003'` |
| Arrow Up | `'\uE013'` |
| Arrow Down | `'\uE015'` |

---

## Common Mistakes

| ❌ Wrong | ✅ Correct | Why |
|----------|-----------|-----|
| `element.click()` | `obj.DoClick()` | Browser DOM APIs don't work in Rapise context |
| `element.textContent` | `obj.GetText()` | Use Rapise wrapper methods |
| `element.getAttribute("href")` | `obj._DoDOMGetAttribute("href")` | DOM access via wrappers |
| `Sleep(1000)` | `Global.DoSleep(1000)` | `Global` object required |
| `obj._DoDOMQueryXPath("//button")` | `obj._DoDOMQueryXPath(".//button")` | Relative XPath must start with `.` |
| `Navigator.SeSFind()` for optional elements | `Navigator.Find()` | `SeSFind` fails test; `Find` returns null |
| `Tester.Assert()` in `Do`-prefixed functions | Return `false` | `Do` functions auto-report; `false` = failure |
| `obj.DoClick()` inside page object methods | `obj._DoClick()` | Underscore avoids duplicate reporting |

---

## Best Practices

1. **Set object_name** before actions for readable reports
2. **Use _DoEnsureVisible()** before clicking off-screen elements
3. **Use Navigator.Find** for optional elements, **Navigator.SeSFind** for required
4. **Disable WebDriver.autoWait** for file uploads and stable-page actions
5. **Use relative XPath starting with `.`** in _DoDOMQueryXPath
6. **Prefer multi-strategy XPaths** joined with `|` for robustness:

```javascript
var xpath = "//button[@name='" + name + "']"
    + "|//button[text()='" + name + "']"
    + "|//button[@title='" + name + "']";
```

================================================================================

# Rapise Visual Language (RVL)

RVL is a spreadsheet-based test scripting language. Tests are written in Excel files (`.rvl.xlsx`) with a structured 7-column format.

## RVL Structure

Every RVL script has exactly 7 columns:

| Flow | Type | Object | Action | ParamName | ParamType | ParamValue |
|------|------|--------|--------|-----------|-----------|------------|

- **Flow**: Control flow keywords (If, ElseIf, Else, Loop, End, Map, #, /*, */, ?, And, Or)
- **Type**: Row type (Action, Variable, Param, Condition, Assert, Rows, Range, Database)
- **Object**: Object ID or map name
- **Action**: Method to call or condition type
- **ParamName**: Parameter name
- **ParamType**: Data type (string, number, boolean, variable, expression)
- **ParamValue**: Parameter value

---

## Comments

Single-line comment (# in Flow column):

| Flow | Type | Object | Action | ParamName | ParamType | ParamValue |
|------|------|--------|--------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| # | This is a comment | | | | | |

Multi-line comment:

| Flow | Type | Object | Action | ParamName | ParamType | ParamValue |
|------|------|--------|--------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| /* | Start of multi-line comment | | | | | |
| | Line 2 of comment | | | | | |
| */ | | | | | | |

---

## Actions

Call an object method. Every action stores its return value in the built-in `LastResult` variable, which can be used by the next action.

| Flow | Type | Object | Action | ParamName | ParamType | ParamValue |
|------|------|--------|--------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| | Action | LoginButton | DoClick | | | |

Action with parameters:

| Flow | Type | Object | Action | ParamName | ParamType | ParamValue |
|------|------|--------|--------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| | Action | UsernameField | DoSetText | txt | string | admin |

Action with multiple parameters (additional params on Param rows):

| Flow | Type | Object | Action | ParamName | ParamType | ParamValue |
|------|------|--------|--------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| | Action | Global | DoLaunch | cmdLine | string | notepad.exe |
| | Param | | | wrkDir | string | C:\Temp |

Using LastResult from previous action:

| Flow | Type | Object | Action | ParamName | ParamType | ParamValue |
|------|------|--------|--------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| | Action | MyField | GetText | | | |
| | Action | Tester | Message | message | variable | LastResult |

### Conditional Action

`?` in Flow column - action only runs if object exists:

| Flow | Type | Object | Action | ParamName | ParamType | ParamValue |
|------|------|--------|--------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| ? | Action | OptionalPopup | DoClick | | | |

---

## Variables

### Local Variable

| Flow | Type | Object | Action | ParamName | ParamType | ParamValue |
|------|------|--------|--------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| | Variable | | | myVar | string | Hello |

### Global Variable (with default)

| Flow | Type | Object | Action | ParamName | ParamType | ParamValue |
|------|------|--------|--------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| | Variable | | Global | myGlobal | | |
| | Param | | | defaultValue | string | DefaultText |

### Using Variables

Reference variables with `variable` as ParamType:

| Flow | Type | Object | Action | ParamName | ParamType | ParamValue |
|------|------|--------|--------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| | Action | TextField | DoSetText | txt | variable | myVar |

---

## Conditions (If/ElseIf/Else)

### Simple If

| Flow | Type | Object | Action | ParamName | ParamType | ParamValue |
|------|------|--------|--------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| If | Param | | | param1 | variable | status |
| | Condition | | param1 == param2 | | | |
| | Param | | | param2 | string | active |
| # | Actions when status equals "active" | | | | | |
| | Action | ActivePanel | DoClick | | | |
| End | of If | | | | | |

### If-Else

| Flow | Type | Object | Action | ParamName | ParamType | ParamValue |
|------|------|--------|--------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| If | Param | | | param1 | number | count |
| | Condition | | param1 > param2 | | | |
| | Param | | | param2 | number | 0 |
| # | Count is positive | | | | | |
| | Action | Tester | Message | message | string | Has items |
| Else | | | | | | |
| # | Count is zero or negative | | | | | |
| | Action | Tester | Message | message | string | No items |
| End | of Else | | | | | |

### If-ElseIf

| Flow | Type | Object | Action | ParamName | ParamType | ParamValue |
|------|------|--------|--------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| If | Param | | | param1 | variable | mode |
| | Condition | | param1 == param2 | | | |
| | Param | | | param2 | string | create |
| # | Create mode | | | | | |
| ElseIf | Param | | | param1 | variable | mode |
| | Condition | | param1 == param2 | | | |
| | Param | | | param2 | string | edit |
| # | Edit mode | | | | | |
| End | of ElseIf | | | | | |

### Condition Operators

**Binary conditions:**
- `param1 == param2` - equals
- `param1 != param2` - not equals
- `param1 > param2` - greater than
- `param1 >= param2` - greater or equal
- `param1 < param2` - less than
- `param1 <= param2` - less or equal
- `param1 contains param2` - substring check

**Unary conditions:**
- `param1 IsTrue` - checks if true
- `param1 IsFalse` - checks if false
- `param1 IsNull` - checks if null
- `param1 IsNotNull` - checks if not null
- `param1 IsSet` - checks if has a value (not null/empty/0/false)
- `param1 IsNotSet` - checks if empty/null/0/false

### And/Or Conditions

| Flow | Type | Object | Action | ParamName | ParamType | ParamValue |
|------|------|--------|--------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| If | Param | | | param1 | variable | a |
| | Condition | | param1 > param2 | | | |
| | Param | | | param2 | number | 0 |
| And | Param | | | param1 | variable | b |
| | Condition | | param1 < param2 | | | |
| | Param | | | param2 | number | 100 |
| # | Both conditions true | | | | | |
| End | of If | | | | | |

---

## Loops

### Loop Through Map

| Flow | Type | Object | Action | ParamName | ParamType | ParamValue |
|------|------|--------|--------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| Loop | Map | MyData | | | | |
| # | Loop body - runs once per row | | | | | |
| | Action | Tester | Message | message | MyData | Name |
| End | of Loop | | | | | |

### Loop with Counter (for i = 1 to 10)

| Flow | Type | Object | Action | ParamName | ParamType | ParamValue |
|------|------|--------|--------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| Loop | Variable | i | | from | number | 1 |
| | Param | | | to | number | 10 |
| # | Loop body - i goes from 1 to 10 | | | | | |
| End | of Loop | | | | | |

### While Loop (with condition)

| Flow | Type | Object | Action | ParamName | ParamType | ParamValue |
|------|------|--------|--------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| Loop | Param | | | param1 | variable | counter |
| | Condition | | param1 < param2 | | | |
| | Param | | | param2 | number | 5 |
| # | Loop while counter < 5 | | | | | |
| End | of Loop | | | | | |

---

## Maps (Data Tables)

### Inline Map

| Flow | Type | Object | Action | ParamName | ParamType | ParamValue |
|------|------|--------|--------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| Map | Rows | TestData | | | | |
| | Username | Password | Expected | | | |
| | admin | admin123 | success | | | |
| | user | user456 | success | | | |
| | invalid | wrong | failure | | | |
| End | of Map | | | | | |

### Map from Excel File

| Flow | Type | Object | Action | ParamName | ParamType | ParamValue |
|------|------|--------|--------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| Map | Range | TestData | | fileName | string | %WORKDIR%\Data.xlsx |
| | Param | | | sheetName | string | Sheet1 |
| End | of Map | | | | | |

### Using Map Data in Loop

| Flow | Type | Object | Action | ParamName | ParamType | ParamValue |
|------|------|--------|--------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| Loop | Map | TestData | | | | |
| | Action | UsernameField | DoSetText | txt | TestData | Username |
| | Action | PasswordField | DoSetText | txt | TestData | Password |
| | Action | LoginButton | DoClick | | | |
| End | of Loop | | | | | |

---

## Assertions

| Flow | Type | Object | Action | ParamName | ParamType | ParamValue |
|------|------|--------|--------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| | Assert | | | message | string | Values match |
| | Param | | | param1 | variable | actual |
| | Condition | | param1 == param2 | | | |
| | Param | | | param2 | string | expected |

## Calling JavaScript Functions

Define functions in `User.js`, call them from RVL via `Functions` object:

```javascript
// In User.js
function CalculateTotal(price, qty) {
    return price * qty;
}
```

| Flow | Type | Object | Action | ParamName | ParamType | ParamValue |
|------|------|--------|--------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| | Action | Functions | CalculateTotal | price | number | 10 |
| | Param | | | qty | number | 5 |

Result is stored in `LastResult` variable.

---

## RVL-JavaScript Interop

### Running RVL from JavaScript

```javascript
// In Main.js
function Test(params)
{
    RVL.DoPlayScript("Main.rvl.xlsx");
}

// Run specific sheet
RVL.DoPlayScript("Main.rvl.xlsx", "LoginSheet");
```

### Passing Parameters

```javascript
// Pass params to RVL
RVL.DoPlayScript("Main.rvl.xlsx", "TestSheet", {
    username: "admin",
    environment: "staging"
});
```

Access in RVL using Global variables.

## ParamType Reference

| ParamType | Description | Example |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| string | Text value | Hello World |
| number | Numeric value | 42 |
| boolean | true/false | true |
| variable | Reference to variable | myVar |
| expression | JavaScript expression | price * 1.1 |
| *MapName* | Value from map column | TestData |

## Common Patterns

### Data-Driven Login Test

| Flow | Type | Object | Action | ParamName | ParamType | ParamValue |
|------|------|--------|--------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| Map | Rows | Logins | | | | |
| | User | Pass | Expected | | | |
| | admin | pwd1 | success | | | |
| | guest | pwd2 | failure | | | |
| End | of Map | | | | | |
| Loop | Map | Logins | | | | |
| | Action | UsernameField | DoSetText | txt | Logins | User |
| | Action | PasswordField | DoSetText | txt | Logins | Pass |
| | Action | LoginButton | DoClick | | | |
| | Action | Global | DoSleep | millis | number | 2000 |
| # | Verify result | | | | | |
| End | of Loop | | | | | |

### Conditional Cleanup

| Flow | Type | Object | Action | ParamName | ParamType | ParamValue |
|------|------|--------|--------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| ? | Action | ClosePopup | DoClick | | | |
| ? | Action | CancelDialog | DoClick | | | |

# Rapise Test Framework Structure

This document describes the file and folder structure of Rapise test frameworks.

## Framework Root Structure

```
MyFramework/
├── Framework.sstest          # Main framework file (open this in Rapise)
├── Main.js                   # Framework entry point
├── Objects.js                # Framework-level learned objects
├── Common.js                 # Shared utility functions
├── TestCases/                # Test case folders
├── PageObjects/              # Page object modules
├── Lib/LibFramework/         # Framework configuration (Parameters.json, Framework.json)
├── Shared/                   # Shared config and data (Common.rvl.xlsx)
├── AI/                       # AI-related files
├── Profiles/                 # Browser/device profiles
└── Reports/                  # Execution reports
```

---

## Test Case Structure

Each test case is a folder containing:

```
TestCases/
└── Login Test/
    ├── Test.sstest           # Test case file
    ├── Main.js               # Test entry point
    ├── Main.rvl.xlsx         # RVL script (if using RVL)
    ├── Objects.js            # Test-specific learned objects
    ├── User.js               # Custom JavaScript functions
    ├── ai.commands.json      # AI-generated command mappings
    └── Reports/              # Test execution reports
```

### Main.js

Entry point that Rapise calls when executing the test:

```javascript
function Test(params)
{
    // For RVL-based tests
    RVL.DoPlayScript("Main.rvl.xlsx", Tester.GetParam("sheetName", "RVL"));
}

// Libraries to load (comma-separated)
g_load_libraries = ["Web"];
```

### Objects.js

Contains learned UI objects:

```javascript
saved_script_objects = {
    "LoginButton": {
        "version": 0,
        "object_type": "HTMLObject",
        "object_name": "Login Button",
        "object_library": "Chrome HTML",
        "xpath": "//button[@id='login']",
        "title": "Login Page",
        "url": "https://example.com/login"
    },
    "UsernameField": {
        "version": 0,
        "object_type": "HTMLObject",
        "object_name": "Username",
        "xpath": "//input[@name='username']"
    }
};
```

Access objects in tests:

```javascript
SeS("LoginButton").DoClick();
SeS("UsernameField").DoSetText("admin");
```

### User.js

Custom functions available in both JavaScript and RVL:

```javascript
function Login(username, password) {
    SeS("UsernameField").DoSetText(username);
    SeS("PasswordField").DoSetText(password);
    SeS("LoginButton").DoClick();
    Global.DoSleep(2000);
}

function VerifyLoggedIn() {
    var welcome = SeS("WelcomeMessage");
    return welcome && welcome.GetText().indexOf("Welcome") >= 0;
}
```

---

## Page Objects

Reusable UI component modules:

```
PageObjects/
└── MyApp/
    ├── Test.sstest           # Page object file
    ├── Main.js               # Entry point (for testing page object)
    ├── MyApp.js              # Page object implementation
    ├── Objects.js            # Learned objects for this page
    └── User.js               # Helper functions
```

### Page Object Implementation (MyApp.js)

Functions starting with `Do` are auto-reported as actions. Returning `false` automatically fails the action (no `Tester.Assert` needed). Use underscore methods (`_DoClick`, `_DoSetText`) inside to avoid duplicate report entries.

```javascript
SeSPageObject("MyApp");

/**
 * Logs into the application
 * @param username User name
 * @param password User password
 */
function MyApp_DoLogin(/**string*/ username, /**string*/ password)
{
    // Underscore methods: don't double-report since DoLogin is already reported
    SeS("UsernameField")._DoSetText(username);
    SeS("PasswordField")._DoSetText(password);
    SeS("LoginButton")._DoClick();
    Global.DoSleep(2000);
    return true;
}

/**
 * Clicks a button by name
 * @param name Button label or name attribute
 */
function MyApp_DoClickButton(/**string*/ name)
{
    var xpath = "//button[@name='" + name + "']"
        + "|//button[normalize-space(.)='" + name + "']";
    var obj = Navigator.SeSFind(xpath);
    if (obj) {
        obj.object_name = name;  // Shows "Save" instead of XPath in report
        return obj._DoClick();   // Underscore: don't double-report
    }
    return false;  // Returning false fails the DoClickButton action
}
```

Usage in tests:

```javascript
MyApp.DoLogin("admin", "password123");
MyApp.DoClickButton("Save");
```

### RVL-Based Page Objects

Page objects can also be created using RVL instead of JavaScript. RVL is recommended for straightforward scenarios involving UI interactions. JavaScript is better for complex logic, loops, data manipulation, or web service interactions.

**Folder structure:**

```
PageObjects/
└── App/
    ├── Test.sstest           # Page object file
    ├── Main.js               # Entry point
    ├── Main.rvl.xlsx         # RVL actions (sheets = actions)
    ├── App.js                # Auto-generated JS wrapper
    ├── Objects.js            # Learned objects
    └── User.js               # Helper functions
```

**Key difference from JS-based:** In RVL mode, each **sheet** (except `RVL` and `PageObject`) becomes an action. The sheet name is the action name.

**Main.rvl.xlsx sheets:**

| Sheet | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `RVL` | Default sheet, typically empty or contains internal tests (required) |
| `PageObject` | Contains action description shown in tooltips (required) |
| `DoLogin` | Example action sheet - becomes `App.DoLogin()` |
| `DoLogout` | Example action sheet - becomes `App.DoLogout()` |
| `DoNavigate` | Example action sheet - becomes `App.DoNavigate()` |

Users can define as many action sheets as needed with different names. The `RVL` and `PageObject` sheets are always required. Every other sheet defines an action of the Page Object.

**Action Parameters in RVL:**

Define parameters in the sheet name using signatures:

```
DoLogin(/**string*/usr, /**string*/pwd)
DoAdd(name=Jim, age=41)
```

Supported parameter types: `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `object`.

**Inside an RVL action sheet:**

| Flow | Type | Object | Action | ParamName | ParamType | ParamValue |
|------|------|--------|--------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| # | DoLogin description | | | | | |
| | Variable | | | usr | string | TBD |
| | Variable | | | pwd | string | TBD |
| | Variable | | | ReturnValue | | |
| # | Action steps below | | | | | |
| | Action | UsernameField | DoSetText | txt | variable | usr |
| | Action | PasswordField | DoSetText | txt | variable | pwd |
| | Action | LoginButton | DoClick | | | |

Variables before `ReturnValue` are parameters. Assign `ReturnValue` during execution to return a value.

**Auto-generated wrapper (App.js):**

Rapise auto-generates JavaScript wrappers for RVL actions:

```javascript
//<autogenerated> - Don't edit!
function App_DoLogin(/**string*/usr, /**string*/pwd)
{
    var res = SeSPageObjectRvlInvoke(
        this,
        __dirname+"\\Test.sstest",
        __dirname+"\\Main.rvl.xlsx",
        "DoLogin",
        { usr: usr, pwd: pwd }
    );
    return res;
}
global.App_DoLogin = App_DoLogin;

SeSPageObject("App");
```

**Usage (same as JS-based):**

```javascript
// In JavaScript
App.DoLogin("admin", "password123");
```

| Flow | Type | Object | Action | ParamName | ParamType | ParamValue |
|------|------|--------|--------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| | Action | App | DoLogin | usr | string | admin |
| | Param | | | pwd | string | password123 |

---

## Shared Configuration

### Shared/Common.rvl.xlsx

Special workbook for framework-wide RVL definitions. All variables, maps, and repositories declared here are automatically available in every RVL sheet across the entire framework.

**Key characteristics:**
- One per framework, located in `Shared/` folder
- All sheets are treated as preambles (no actions, only definitions)
- Variables, maps, and repositories become globally available
- Create via Object tree → Shared → New Common.rvl.xlsx

**Example Common.rvl.xlsx content:**

| Flow | Type | Object | Action | ParamName | ParamType | ParamValue |
|------|------|--------|--------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| # | Global Variables | | | | | |
| | Variable | | | g_baseUrl | string | https://example.com |
| | Variable | | | g_timeout | number | 30000 |

Variables in Common.rvl.xlsx are global by default - no need for the `Global` keyword. They are accessible from any RVL sheet or JavaScript code in the framework.

---

## Framework Configuration (Lib/LibFramework)

Framework settings are stored in `Lib/LibFramework/`:

```
Lib/LibFramework/
├── Framework.json            # Test cases, page objects, test sets structure
├── Parameters.json           # Framework parameters with default values
├── Spira.json                # Spira integration mappings (optional)
└── LibFramework.js           # Framework library code
```

### Parameters.json

Defines framework-wide parameters accessible in all test cases:

```json
{
  "params": [
    { "name": "Browser", "type": "browser", "defaultValue": "Selenium - Chrome" },
    { "name": "EnvURL", "type": "string", "defaultValue": "https://dev.example.com" },
    { "name": "Username", "type": "string", "defaultValue": "admin" },
    { "name": "Password", "type": "password", "defaultValue": "encryptedValue==" }
  ],
  "configs": [
    { "id": "default1", "name": "Default" },
    { "id": "staging1", "name": "Staging", "values": { "EnvURL": "https://staging.example.com" } }
  ]
}
```

**Parameter types:** `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `password`, `select`, `browser`, `mobile`, `datacolumn`, `environment`.

**Configurations:** Named sets of parameter overrides. Only parameters that differ from defaults are specified in the `values` object.

**Accessing parameters:**

In JavaScript:
```javascript
var url = Tester.GetParam("EnvURL");
```

In RVL (use `testparam` as ParamType):

| Flow | Type | Object | Action | ParamName | ParamType | ParamValue |
|------|------|--------|--------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| | Action | Navigator | Open | url | testparam | EnvURL |

### Framework.json

Contains framework structure. Managed by Rapise IDE - typically not edited manually.

```json
{
  "framework": { ... },      // Framework metadata and settings
  "testcases": [             // List of test cases
    { "id": "ABC123", "name": "LoginTest", "alias": "Login Test",
      "sstest": "%WORKDIR%TestCases\\LoginTest\\Test.sstest",
      "rep": "%WORKDIR%TestCases\\LoginTest\\Objects.js",
      "libraries": ["Web"] }
  ],
  "pageobjects": {           // Page objects
    "MyApp": { "id": "XYZ789", "js": "%WORKDIR%PageObjects\\MyApp\\MyApp.js",
      "sstest": "%WORKDIR%PageObjects\\MyApp\\Test.sstest",
      "rep": "%WORKDIR%PageObjects\\MyApp\\Objects.js",
      "libraries": ["Web"] }
  },
  "testsets": [ ... ],       // Test sets grouping test cases with configs
  "shared": [ ... ]          // Shared JavaScript files
}
```

### Spira.json

Maps framework elements to SpiraTest for CI/CD integration. Managed by Rapise IDE - typically not edited manually.

```json
{
  "projectId": 9,            // Spira project ID
  "testCasesFolderId": 755,  // Test cases folder in Spira
  "testSetsFolderId": 351,   // Test sets folder in Spira
  "testcases": [             // Rapise ID to Spira ID mappings
    { "id": "ABC123", "spiraId": 7081 }
  ],
  "testsets": [              // Rapise ID to Spira ID mappings
    { "id": "a448ba14", "spiraId": 1041 }
  ]
}
```

### Shared/Config.xlsx

Excel file storing configuration values:

| Key | Value |
|-----|-------|
| BaseUrl | https://example.com |
| Username | testuser |
| Password | (encrypted) |
| Timeout | 30000 |

Access in code:

```javascript
var url = Global.GetProperty("BaseUrl", "", "%WORKDIR%\\Shared\\Config.xlsx");
var user = Global.GetProperty("Username", "", "%WORKDIR%\\Shared\\Config.xlsx");
```

---

## AI Integration Files

### Shared/AIExamples.txt (or AI/AIExamples.txt)

Contains positive and negative examples for AI code generation. When generating code, the AI uses these examples to learn preferred patterns and avoid incorrect approaches.

**Purpose:**
- **Positive examples** (thumbs up): Correct code patterns the AI should follow
- **Negative examples** (thumbs down): Incorrect approaches the AI should avoid

**Format:**

```
Prompt: Write OS type to the report
Correct: Tester.Message("OS Type: ", Global.GetOsType());

Prompt: Wait 1 second
Wrong: Sleep(1);

Prompt: Wait 1 second
Correct: Global.DoSleep(1000);
```

Examples are added via thumbs up/down buttons in the AI Panel, or manually edited. Rapise checks both `%WORKDIR%/AI` and `%WORKDIR%/Shared` folders.

### Shared/AiPrompt.txt (or AI/AiPrompt.txt)

Framework-specific instructions appended to every AI code generation request. Used to enforce conventions and provide guidance.

```
## Button Clicks
Use MyApp.DoClickButton(name) for clicking buttons.
CRITICAL: Do not click disabled buttons.

## Form Fields
Use MyApp.DoSetField(name, value) for text inputs.
Use MyApp.DoSelectDropdown(name, option) for dropdowns.

## Before Calculations
Always press Clear button before starting a new calculation.
```

### ai.commands.json (per test case)

Maps AI command prompts to their generated JavaScript code. Created automatically when AI commands are processed.

```json
{
  "ABC1-DEF2-GH34": {
    "prompt": "Click the Save button",
    "code": [
      "MyApp.DoClickButton(\"Save\");"
    ]
  }
}
```

Once code is generated and cached, test execution does not require AI access.

---

## SeS() Object Access

`SeS(objectId)` retrieves learned objects from Objects.js:

```javascript
// Standard action - logs to report, fails test on error
SeS("SaveButton").DoClick();

// Silent action (underscore prefix) - no report, no failure
SeS("OptionalPopup")._DoClick();
```

### Underscore Convention

For actions starting with `Do`:
- `DoClick()` - Reports action, fails test if error
- `_DoClick()` - Silent, returns false on error

**Use underscore for:**
- Optional elements that may not exist
- Intermediate navigation steps
- Cleanup actions

**Use regular for:**
- Critical test actions
- Verifications
- Final meaningful interactions

---

## Library Loading

### g_load_libraries

Specifies which libraries to load:

```javascript
// Single library
g_load_libraries = ["Web"];

// Multiple libraries
g_load_libraries = ["Web", "DomSalesforce"];

// Desktop application
g_load_libraries = ["UIAutomation"];
```

Common libraries:
- `Web` - Selenium/Chrome web testing
- `UIAutomation` - Windows UI Automation
- `DomSalesforce` - Salesforce Lightning components
- `DomDynamicsCrm` - Microsoft Dynamics CRM
- `Mobile` - Appium mobile testing

---

## File Reference Summary

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `*.sstest` | Rapise project file (open in Rapise) |
| `Main.js` | Test entry point, contains Test() function |
| `Main.rvl.xlsx` | RVL script (spreadsheet-based test) |
| `Objects.js` | Learned UI objects |
| `User.js` | Custom JavaScript functions |
| `Common.js` | Framework-wide shared functions |
| `Lib/LibFramework/Parameters.json` | Framework parameters (environment, credentials) |
| `Lib/LibFramework/Framework.json` | Framework structure (test cases, page objects) |
| `Shared/Common.rvl.xlsx` | Global RVL variables and maps |
| `ai.commands.json` | AI-generated code mappings |
| `AiPrompt.txt` | AI guidance for code generation |
| `AIExamples.txt` | Positive/negative examples for AI |

---

## Creating New Test Cases

1. Create folder under `TestCases/`
2. Copy `Test.sstest` template
3. Create `Main.js` with `Test()` function
4. Create `Objects.js` (or learn objects via Rapise)
5. Optionally create `Main.rvl.xlsx` for RVL tests
6. Add `User.js` for custom functions

```javascript
// Minimal Main.js
function Test(params)
{
    Tester.Message("Starting test");
    // Your test code here
}

g_load_libraries = ["Web"];
```

---

## Best Practices

1. **Organize by feature**: Group related test cases in subfolders
2. **Use page objects**: Extract reusable UI patterns
3. **Centralize config**: Use `Parameters.json` for environment-specific values, `Common.rvl.xlsx` for RVL global variables
4. **Name objects descriptively**: `LoginButton` not `Button1`
5. **Keep AI files updated**: Maintain AiPrompt.txt for accurate AI assistance
6. **Use underscore for optional elements**: Prevent false test failures

================================================================================

# Extending Rapise

This document covers two ways to extend Rapise functionality:
1. **Page Objects** - High-level reusable actions (e.g., `MyApp.Launch()`, `MyApp.DoLogin()`)
2. **Extension Libraries** - Custom control types for recording/playback (e.g., `DomMyAppGrid`)

---

## Page Objects

Page objects provide high-level, reusable actions accessed as `PageObjectName.ActionName()` (e.g., `MyApp.DoLogin(user, pwd)`, `MyApp.DoClickButton("Save")`). They encapsulate complex UI interactions into simple method calls.

### Structure

```
PageObjects/
└── MyApp/
    ├── Test.sstest           # Page object file
    ├── Main.js               # Entry point
    ├── MyApp.js              # Page object implementation
    ├── Objects.js            # Learned objects
    └── User.js               # Helper functions
```

### Implementation Pattern

Functions starting with `Do` are auto-reported as actions. Returning `false` automatically fails the action (no `Tester.Assert` needed). Use underscore methods (`_DoClick`, `_DoSetText`) inside to avoid duplicate report entries.

```javascript
/**
 * @PageObject MyApp - Common application actions
 */
SeSPageObject("MyApp");

/**
 * Clicks a button by name.
 * @param name Button label
 */
function MyApp_DoClickButton(/**string*/ name)
{
    var xpath = "//button[@name='" + name + "']"
        + "|//button[normalize-space(.)='" + name + "']";
    var obj = Navigator.SeSFind(xpath);
    if (obj) {
        obj.object_name = name;   // Shows "Save" instead of XPath in report
        return obj._DoClick();    // Underscore: don't double-report
    }
    return false;  // Returning false fails the DoClickButton action
}

/**
 * Sets a form field value.
 * @param name Field label
 * @param value Text to enter
 */
function MyApp_DoSetTextField(/**string*/ name, /**string*/ value)
{
    var xpath = "//input[@id=//label[normalize-space(.)='" + name + "']/@for]";
    var obj = Navigator.SeSFind(xpath);
    if (obj) {
        obj.object_name = name;
        return obj._DoSetText(value);
    }
    return false;
}
```

### Usage

In JavaScript:
```javascript
MyApp.DoClickButton("Save");
MyApp.DoSetTextField("Company", "Acme Corp");
```

In RVL:

| Flow | Type | Object | Action | ParamName | ParamType | ParamValue |
|------|------|--------|--------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| | Action | MyApp | DoClickButton | name | string | Save |
| | Action | MyApp | DoSetTextField | name | string | Company |
| | Param | | | value | string | Acme Corp |

### Best Practices

1. **Naming**: Use `PageObjectName_DoActionName` function pattern (e.g., `MyApp_DoLogin` becomes `MyApp.DoLogin()`)
2. **Do prefix**: Functions starting with `Do` are auto-reported; returning `false` fails the action
3. **Underscore methods**: Use `_DoClick()`, `_DoSetText()` inside to avoid duplicate report entries
4. **JSDoc comments**: Add `@param` annotations for auto-completion
5. **object_name**: Set before actions for readable reports
6. **Multi-strategy XPaths**: Use `|` to join multiple locators
7. **Configuration**: Read settings via `Tester.GetParam()` or `Global.GetProperty()`

---

## Extension Libraries (Custom Controls)

Extension libraries add support for application-specific controls (grids, comboboxes, etc.) that can be learned and recorded. The library code runs during **playback** in the Rapise test engine context.

### Library Structure

```
Lib/LibDomMyApp/
├── LibDomMyApp.js            # Main library, plugin registration
├── LibDomMyAppRules.js       # Control type rules (SeSRegisterRule)
├── LibDomMyAppInfo.js        # Documentation metadata
├── LibDomMyAppRecorder.js    # Recording hooks (optional)
├── DomMyAppGrid.js           # Grid control behavior
├── DomMyAppComboBox.js       # ComboBox control behavior
└── ...                       # Additional control files
```

### Main Library File (LibDomMyApp.js)

```javascript
/**
 * @fileOverview DomMyApp library - custom controls for MyApp
 */

DomMyAppPlugin = {
    pluginId: "DomMyAppPlugin",
    include: "Lib/LibDomMyApp/LibDomMyAppRecorder.js",
    attachFunctionName: "DomMyAppPluginAttach",
    
    Init: function() {
        return true;
    }
}

eval(g_helper.IncludeOnce("Lib/LibDomMyApp/LibDomMyAppRules.js"));

// Optional: XPath modification callback
function DomMyApp_OnXPathNotFound(xpath) {
    // Modify xpath to handle dynamic IDs
    return xpath;
}
g_xpathNotFoundCallbacks.push(DomMyApp_OnXPathNotFound);

// Optional: Web app profile for recording
var DomMyApp_WebAppProfile = {
    record: {
        attributes: [
            { name: "id", notEmpty: true, exclude: "\\d" },
            { name: "name" },
            { name: "aria-label" },
            { name: "data-testid" }
        ]
    }
}
g_webAppProfile = DomMyApp_WebAppProfile;
```

### Rules File (LibDomMyAppRules.js)

```javascript
/**
 * @fileOverview Control type rules for MyApp
 */

eval(g_helper.IncludeOnce('Lib/LibDomMyApp/DomMyAppGrid.js'));
eval(g_helper.IncludeOnce('Lib/LibDomMyApp/DomMyAppComboBox.js'));

/** @rule DomMyAppGrid */
SeSRegisterRule({
    rule_id: "DomMyAppGridRule",
    object_type: "DomMyAppGrid",
    object_flavor: "Grid",
    extend_rule: "HTMLObject",
    dont_hash: true,
    behavior: ["DomMyAppGridBehavior"]
});

/** @rule DomMyAppComboBox */
SeSRegisterRule({
    rule_id: "DomMyAppComboBoxRule",
    object_type: "DomMyAppComboBox",
    object_flavor: "ComboBox",
    extend_rule: "HTMLObject",
    dont_hash: true,
    behavior: ["DomMyAppComboBoxBehavior"]
});
```

### Control Behavior File (DomMyAppComboBox.js)

```javascript
/** @behavior DomMyAppComboBox */
SeSRegisterBehavior({
    id: "DomMyAppComboBoxBehavior",
    
    actions: [
        {
            actionName: "SelectItem",
            /** @action */
            DoAction: DomMyAppComboBox_DoSelectItem
        }
    ],
    
    properties: {
        // Define properties if needed
    }
});

/**
 * Selects an item from the combobox.
 * @param item Item text or index
 */
function DomMyAppComboBox_DoSelectItem(/**string|number*/ item)
{
    // Open dropdown
    var trigger = this._DoDOMQueryXPath(".//button[@aria-haspopup='true']");
    if (trigger && trigger.length > 0) {
        trigger[0]._DoClick();
        Global.DoSleep(500);
        
        // Find and click item
        var itemEl = this._DoDOMQueryXPath(".//li[@role='option' and contains(.,'" + item + "')]");
        if (itemEl && itemEl.length > 0) {
            itemEl[0]._DoClick();
            return true;
        }
    }
    return false;
}
```

### Info File (LibDomMyAppInfo.js)

```javascript
if (typeof(g_libInfo) == "undefined") g_libInfo = {};

g_libInfo.DomMyAppComboBoxRuleInfo = {
    _description: "MyApp ComboBox control behavior."
}

g_libInfo.DomMyAppComboBoxBehaviorInfo = {
    _description: "Behavior for MyApp ComboBox controls.",
    actions: {
        SelectItem: {
            _description: "Selects an item from the dropdown.",
            item: {
                description: "Item text or index to select.",
                type: "string|number"
            }
        }
    },
    properties: {}
}
```

### Recorder File (LibDomMyAppRecorder.js)

The recorder file runs **inside the browser context** (not the Rapise test engine). It intercepts user actions during recording and maps them to custom control types and actions.

Since it runs in the browser, you can use standard DOM APIs (`element.tagName`, `element.innerText`, `el.parentNode`, etc.) plus Rapise-provided helper functions.

```javascript
// Entry point - called by Rapise during recording
function DomMyAppPluginAttach(browser, actionHolder)
{
    if(l2) Log2("DomMyApp Plugin Initializing");
    
    // Return codes
    var R_NOT_OBJECT = 0;    // Element not recognized by this plugin
    var R_ACTION_FOUND = 1;  // Object and action identified
    var R_OBJECT_FOUND = 2;  // Object identified, but action unknown
    
    // Console fallback for browsers without console
    if (typeof(console) == "undefined")
    {
        var console = {};
        console.log = function(msg){};
    }
    
    // Utility to clean object names (remove dynamic IDs)
    function _normalizeObjectName(t)
    {
        t = t || "";
        var re = new RegExp("_[0-9]+_", "ig");
        t = t.replace(re, "_");
        return t;
    }
    
    //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
    // Control detection functions
    //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
    
    function IsDomMyAppGrid(evt, element, eventOpts, objName, description, flavor, items)
    {
        // Helper to extract cell info from clicked element
        function _getCell(el)
        {
            var cell = { row: 0, col: 0 };
            var cellEl = __hasParentWithTag(el, "td");
            if (cellEl)
            {
                // Get column index and name from header
                var colNum = __doDOMQueryXPath(cellEl, "count(./preceding-sibling::td)", true);
                var colEl = __doDOMQueryXPath(root, ".//thead/tr/th[" + (colNum + 1) + "]");
                if (colEl && colEl.length > 0)
                    cell.col = colEl[0].innerText;
                else
                    cell.col = colNum;
                
                // Get row identifier (cell text or row index)
                cell.row = cellEl.innerText;
                if (!cell.row)
                {
                    var rowEl = __hasParentWithTag(el, "tr");
                    cell.row = __doDOMQueryXPath(rowEl, "count(./preceding-sibling::tr)", true);
                }
            }
            return cell;
        }
        
        var rvalue = { root: null, result: null, rcode: R_NOT_OBJECT };
        
        var root = __hasParentWithAttr(element, 'class', /myapp-grid/ig);
        if (!root) return rvalue;
        
        var res = {
            cancel: false,
            object_flavor: 'Grid',
            object_name: 'Grid',
            object_type: 'DomMyAppGrid',
            description: 'Grid action',
            locator_data: { xpath: SeS_GenerateXPath(root) }
        };
        
        rvalue.result = res;
        rvalue.root = root;
        rvalue.rcode = R_OBJECT_FOUND;
        
        // Learning mode - return object info and bounding rect
        if (evt == "resolveElementDescriptor")
        {
            res.rect = __getElementRect(root);
            res.action = undefined;
            return rvalue;
        }
        
        // Handle Click event
        if (evt == "Click")
        {
            var cell = _getCell(element);
            if (cell)
            {
                var descr = "Click on '" + cell.row + "' in column '" + cell.col + "'";
                res.action = {
                    name: "ClickCell",
                    description: descr,
                    params: [cell.row, cell.col]
                };
            }
            rvalue.rcode = R_ACTION_FOUND;
        }
        
        return rvalue;
    }
    
    //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
    // Main entry point - Rapise calls this for every user action
    //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
    
    actionHolder.OnActionRecorded = function(evt, element, eventOpts, objName, description, flavor, items)
    {
        if (!element) return false;
        
        function _checkDomMyAppControls()
        {
            var r = manageExceptions(IsDomMyAppGrid)(evt, element, eventOpts, objName, description, flavor, items);
            if (r.rcode == R_OBJECT_FOUND || r.rcode == R_ACTION_FOUND)
                return r.result;
            
            // Add more control checks here...
            // var r = manageExceptions(IsDomMyAppComboBox)(evt, element, ...);
            // if (r.rcode == R_OBJECT_FOUND || r.rcode == R_ACTION_FOUND)
            //     return r.result;
        }
        
        // Debug mode vs production mode
        if (typeof(g_debug) != "undefined" && g_debug)
        {
            return _checkDomMyAppControls();
        }
        else
        {
            try
            {
                return _checkDomMyAppControls();
            }
            catch(exc)
            {
                PrintException("DomMyApp Plugin exception", exc);
            }
        }
        return false;
    }
    
    //#region Debug Functions
    function PrintException(title, exc)
    {
        Log("************** " + title + " *********************\n");
        var vDebug = "";
        for (var prop in exc)
        {
            vDebug += "    [" + prop + "]:" + exc[prop] + "\n";
        }
        if (exc && exc.message)
        {
            vDebug += "    [message]:" + exc.message + "\n";
        }
        if (exc && exc.stack)
        {
            vDebug += "    [stack]:" + exc.stack + "\n";
        }
        Log(vDebug);
        Log('**********************************************************');
    }

    function manageExceptions(func)
    {
        var orignal = func;
        var decorated = function()
        {
            function functionName(fn)
            {
                var name = /\W*function\s+([\w\$]+)\(/.exec(fn);
                if (!name) return 'No name';
                return name[1];
            }
            var funcName = functionName(orignal.toString());
            
            if (typeof(g_debug) != "undefined" && g_debug)
            {
                if(l3) Log3("Trying:" + funcName);
                return orignal.apply(this, arguments);
            }
            else
            {
                try
                {
                    return orignal.apply(this, arguments);
                }
                catch(exception)
                {
                    if (!exception.stack)
                        Log("*** Exception in " + funcName + " ***\n");
                    throw exception;
                }
            }
        }
        return decorated;
    }
    //#endregion
}
```

**Recorder Structure Summary:**

1. **Entry function**: `DomMyAppPluginAttach(browser, actionHolder)` - name must match `attachFunctionName` in main library
2. **Return codes**: `R_NOT_OBJECT`, `R_ACTION_FOUND`, `R_OBJECT_FOUND`
3. **Control detection functions**: `IsDomMyAppXxx()` - one per control type, with nested `_getCell()` style helpers
4. **Main handler**: `actionHolder.OnActionRecorded` - entry point called by Rapise
5. **Debug functions**: `PrintException`, `manageExceptions` - for error handling

**Rapise Helper Functions (Browser Context):**

| Function | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `__hasParentWithAttr(el, attr, regex)` | Finds ancestor element with attribute matching regex pattern |
| `__hasParentWithTag(el, tagName)` | Finds ancestor element with specified tag name |
| `__hasParentWithAttrPierceShadowDom(el, attr, regex)` | Same as `__hasParentWithAttr`, but crosses Shadow DOM boundaries |
| `__doDOMQueryXPath(root, xpath, singleValue)` | Executes XPath query; returns array of elements or single numeric value if `singleValue=true` |
| `__getAttribute(el, name)` | Gets element attribute value (returns empty string if not found) |
| `__hasAttribute(el, name)` | Returns true if element has the specified attribute |
| `__getElementRect(el)` | Gets element bounding rectangle `{x, y, w, h, cx, cy}` |
| `__getInnerText(el)` | Cross-browser way to get element's inner text |
| `__isElementVisible(el)` | Checks if element is visible (not `display:none`, `visibility:hidden`, or `opacity:0`) |
| `SeS_GenerateXPath(el)` | Generates XPath locator for element using configured attributes |
| `Log(msg)` | Logging (also `Log1`, `Log2`, `Log3` for different verbosity levels controlled by `l1`, `l2`, `l3` flags) |

**Event Types:**

| Event | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `"Click"` | Mouse click on element |
| `"SetText"` | Text input (`eventOpts` contains the entered text) |
| `"Select"` | Selection from dropdown (`eventOpts` contains selected value) |
| `"resolveElementDescriptor"` | Learning mode - return object info and rect, set `action = undefined` |

**Return Object Structure:**

```javascript
{
    cancel: false,              // true to suppress default recording
    object_flavor: 'Grid',      // Control category (Grid, Button, Edit, ComboBox, List, etc.)
    object_name: 'MyGrid',      // Display name in object repository
    object_type: 'DomMyAppGrid', // Must match SeSRegisterRule object_type
    description: 'Grid action', // Action description for report
    locator_data: {
        xpath: "//div[@class='myapp-grid']"
    },
    rect: { x, y, w, h },       // For resolveElementDescriptor only
    action: {                   // Omit or set undefined for Learn-only
        name: "ClickCell",      // Action method name
        description: "Click cell",
        params: [0, "Column1"]  // Parameters passed to the action
    }
}
```

### Loading the Library

Add to `g_load_libraries` in Main.js:

```javascript
g_load_libraries = ["Web", "DomMyApp"];
```

---

## When to Use Which Approach

| Scenario | Approach |
|----------|----------|
| Reusable high-level actions | Page Object |
| Click button by name, fill forms | Page Object |
| Application-specific workflows | Page Object |
| Custom control types for recording | Extension Library |
| Complex grid/table interactions | Extension Library |
| Application-wide element identification | Extension Library |

**Page Objects** are simpler and sufficient for most automation needs. **Extension Libraries** require deeper knowledge of Rapise internals and are mainly for supporting custom UI frameworks.

---

## Key Functions

### Page Objects

| Function | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `SeSPageObject("Name")` | Registers page object, enables `Name.ActionName()` syntax (e.g., `MyApp.DoLogin()`) |
| `Navigator.SeSFind(xpath)` | Finds element, fails test if not found |
| `Navigator.Find(xpath)` | Finds element, returns null if not found |
| `Navigator.DoWaitFor(xpath, timeout)` | Waits for element |
| `obj._DoDOMQueryXPath(relXpath)` | Finds descendants (xpath must start with `.`) |
| `obj.DoClick()` | Clicks element |
| `obj._DoClick()` | Silent click (no report) |
| `obj.DoSetText(text)` | Sets text value |
| `obj.object_name = "Name"` | Sets display name for reports |

### Extension Libraries (Playback - Rapise Engine Context)

These functions are used in behavior files (e.g., `DomMyAppComboBox.js`) during **playback**. They run in the Rapise test engine, not in the browser.

| Function | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `this._DoDOMQueryXPath(xpath)` | Finds child elements (xpath must start with `.`) |
| `this.GetText()` | Gets element text |
| `this._DoDOMGetAttribute(name)` | Gets DOM attribute |

*Note: Functions like `SeSRegisterRule`, `SeSRegisterBehavior`, and `g_helper.IncludeOnce` are part of the Rapise Engine architecture. They are shown in the library examples above for understanding structure, but users don't call them directly in test code.*
